template.name: startup_idea_review
template.description: Concept validation for an automated IT implementation consulting startup using AI agents. The aim is to probe market potential, feasibility, economics, and go-to-market, and capture concrete next steps.

sections.label: Problem and status quo
sections.description: Pain points in IT implementation consulting today, who feels them, and how teams solve them now (processes, tools, services).

sections.label: Target customers and buyers
sections.description: Ideal customer profiles, segments, priority use cases, the economic buyer vs. users, procurement context, and budget owners.

sections.label: Value proposition and differentiation
sections.description: Specific outcomes the AI-agent approach promises (speed, cost, quality) and what makes it distinct or defensible versus alternatives.

sections.label: Market potential and competition
sections.description: Sizing and growth drivers (TAM/SAM/SOM), timing/urgency, and notable competitors or substitutes the idea would displace.

sections.label: Go-to-market and pilots
sections.description: Acquisition channels, sales motion, partnerships, and concrete pilot or design-partner opportunities and intros.

sections.label: Unit economics and pricing
sections.description: Pricing models, willingness to pay, expected margins, key cost drivers (compute, labor, data), and CAC/LTV considerations.

sections.label: Technical feasibility and data
sections.description: Required capabilities, integrations, data sources and access, accuracy/safety thresholds, and deployment constraints.

sections.label: Risks, regulatory, and operational
sections.description: Major business/technical risks, compliance or security constraints, delivery model considerations, and mitigation or validation experiments.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport
phases.goal: Set context, confirm objectives and timebox, and invite candid feedback.

phases.label: Explore market and problem
phases.goal: Understand the pain, who has it, the size/timing of the opportunity, and current alternatives.

phases.label: Test solution and feasibility
phases.goal: Pressure-test the proposed value prop and the technical/data assumptions; surface major risks.

phases.label: Go-to-market and economics
phases.goal: Map practical paths to early traction and validate pricing and unit economics.

phases.label: Wrap
phases.goal: Confirm takeaways, pilots or intros, and concrete next steps and follow-ups.

issues.description: No explicit section to capture decisions, owners, and concrete next steps, despite the template description saying it will "capture concrete next steps." Relying on wrap + go_to_market_and_pilots risks scattering action items or omitting technical/research follow-ups not tied to pilots.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a section `decisions_and_next_steps` (e.g., "Decisions made, owners, deadlines, follow-ups, intros, and pilot success criteria/milestones."). Update the `wrap` phase `sections_in_focus` to include this new section. To keep 4–8 substantive sections, remove the explicitly-declared `other` (it's auto-appended) or merge two adjacent market sections (e.g., combine `value_proposition_and_differentiation` with `market_potential_and_competition` into `market_and_positioning`).

issues.description: `risks_regulatory_and_operational` is a broad, catch‑all bucket that overlaps with technical/data and GTM. This invites mis-bucketing (e.g., change management vs. compliance vs. delivery model).
issues.suggested_fix: Tighten the description to clearly bound what belongs (e.g., “compliance/security constraints, delivery model risks, liability, SLAs, and validation experiments — exclude adoption/change management which lives in GTM”). Alternatively, split into two clearer facets if you merge other sections to maintain the 4–8 cap.

issues.description: Change management and stakeholder adoption (critical in IT implementations) is not explicitly called out; it may be buried under risks or GTM.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend `go_to_market_and_pilots` description to explicitly include “stakeholder mapping, change management, and adoption plan,” or state in `risks_regulatory_and_operational` what belongs where to avoid ambiguity.

missing_aspects: Decisions and next steps (owners, dates, follow-ups) captured in a dedicated section
Stakeholder adoption and change management for enterprise IT rollouts
Pilot success criteria and KPIs for validation
critique.rationale: Strong, well-paced structure that squarely covers market potential, feasibility, economics, GTM, and risks for an AI-driven IT implementation concept. The main gap is the absence of a dedicated place to record decisions and next actions, which the description explicitly aims to capture. Minor tightening will reduce mis-bucketing around risks and make adoption considerations explicit.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Add a dedicated `decisions_and_next_steps` section and point the `wrap` phase at it; remove the explicitly-declared `other` to keep the section count within 4–8.

template.name: startup_idea_review
template.description: Concept validation for an automated IT implementation consulting startup using AI agents. The aim is to probe market potential, feasibility, economics, and go-to-market, and capture concrete next steps.

sections.label: Problem and status quo
sections.description: Pain points in IT implementation consulting today, who feels them, and how teams solve them now (processes, tools, services).

sections.label: Target customers and buyers
sections.description: Ideal customer profiles, segments, priority use cases, the economic buyer vs. users, procurement context, and budget owners.

sections.label: Market and positioning
sections.description: Specific outcomes the AI-agent approach delivers (speed, cost, quality), how it is differentiated/defensible versus alternatives, and the market context (size, growth drivers, timing, and notable competitors/substitutes).

sections.label: Go-to-market and pilots
sections.description: Acquisition channels, sales motion, partnerships, stakeholder mapping, change management and adoption plan, and concrete pilot/design-partner opportunities, intros, and success criteria/KPIs.

sections.label: Risks, regulatory, and operational

sections.description: Decisions made and open questions, owners, deadlines, required follow-ups (research, technical, customer), requested intros, and pilot milestones/success criteria.

sections.label: Other

phases.label: Explore market and problem
phases.goal: Understand the pain, who has it, the size/timing of the opportunity, and current alternatives.

phases.label: Test solution and feasibility
phases.goal: Pressure-test the proposed value prop and the technical/data assumptions; surface major risks.

phases.label: Go-to-market and economics
phases.goal: Map practical paths to early traction and validate pricing and unit economics.

phases.label: Wrap
phases.goal: Confirm takeaways, pilots or intros, and concrete next steps and follow-ups.

issues.description: No explicit section to define the proposed solution/MVP and operating model. For an “automated IT implementation consulting” idea, the meeting needs a place to capture what the agent(s) actually do, level of automation vs. human-in-the-loop, workflow boundaries, and service vs. product delivery model. Without this, feasibility, economics, and GTM inputs are under-specified and may be mis-bucketed into technical or market sections.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a new section `solution_scope_and_operating_model` (label: "Solution scope and operating model") with description such as: "What the AI agents do end-to-end, MVP scope, boundaries, human-in-the-loop roles and QA/review, delivery model (product vs. service vs. hybrid), and expected service levels." To stay within 8 sections, merge `target_customers_and_buyers` into `market_and_positioning` (rename to `market_customers_and_positioning`) and update phase references accordingly.

issues.description: Overlap on "success criteria/KPIs" between `go_to_market_and_pilots` and `decisions_and_next_steps` may cause filing ambiguity.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep pilot/design-partner success criteria only in `go_to_market_and_pilots`; in `decisions_and_next_steps` focus on owners, deadlines, and follow-ups (remove success criteria wording).

issues.description: `decisions_and_next_steps` is almost always a one-shot end-of-meeting capture; marking it repeated could encourage scattered notes.

missing_aspects: Solution/MVP definition and operating model (AI vs. human-in-the-loop, workflow boundaries, delivery model)
Team/capability prerequisites and gaps (who can build/sell/implement), which is often relevant when asking “what other topics might be relevant?”
critique.rationale: Strong, well-paced structure that covers market potential, feasibility, economics, GTM, and risks for an AI-agent IT consulting concept. However, it lacks an explicit solution/operating-model section, which is core to grounding feasibility, economics, and GTM. Minor overlaps and polish items remain.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Add a clear Solution scope and operating model section and merge with adjacent sections to keep the total substantive sections within 8.

sections.label: Technical feasibility and data
sections.description: Required capabilities and integrations, data sources and access paths, reliability/performance constraints, and deployment architecture and security model needed to make the solution work.

sections.label: Go-to-market and pilots
sections.description: Acquisition channels and sales motion, partnerships and stakeholder mapping, change management and adoption plan, and concrete pilot or design-partner opportunities including intros and pilot success criteria/KPIs.

sections.label: Unit economics and pricing

sections.label: Risks, regulatory, and operational
sections.description: Compliance and security constraints, data governance, delivery model risks, liability and SLAs, auditability and reliability thresholds, and validation or mitigation experiments, excluding adoption/change management (capture under go_to_market_and_pilots) and excluding operating model details (capture under solution_scope_and_operating_model).

sections.label: Decisions and next steps
sections.description: Decisions made and open questions, owners, deadlines, follow-ups needed (research, technical, customer), and requested intros or artifacts to exchange.

phases.label: Go-to-market and economics
phases.goal: Map practical paths to early traction and validate pricing and unit economics.

phases.label: Wrap

issues.description: market_customers_and_positioning and go_to_market_and_pilots both touch stakeholder/procurement mapping, which could yield duplicate notes.
issues.suggested_fix: Confine buyer vs. user roles and procurement context to market_customers_and_positioning, and move all stakeholder mapping to go_to_market_and_pilots; reflect this explicitly in both descriptions.

issues.description: Timeline/milestones for validation (e.g., MVP build, pilot start/end, decision gates) are not explicitly called out.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend decisions_and_next_steps description to include timeline/milestones (e.g., ‘target dates for MVP, pilot kickoff, evaluation window, and go/no-go decision’).

critique.rationale: Strong, well-structured template that maps closely to the user’s goals (market potential, feasibility, economics, challenges) and adds sensible topics like GTM, pilots, and risks. Phases are paced well and sections are concrete and mostly non-overlapping, with clear exclusions to reduce ambiguity. Only minor polish is needed to prevent duplication and to make timelines explicit.
